data.name: Naqid
data.gender_notes: Naqid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic verb 'naqada', meaning 'to inspect, observe, or scrutinize'. In Islamic history, Naqid was a title given to scholars and religious leaders responsible for ensuring the accuracy and authenticity of Islamic texts. The name Naqid carries the meaning “Inspector, observer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Naqid usually hope their child will grow to embody inspector, observer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and truth.
data.etymology: Naqid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Inspector, observer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naqid total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: ناقد
in_arabic.meaning: المُقيم على النقد، الذي يَحكم بين الناس بالعدل
in_arabic.long_meaning: الناقد، هو الشخص الذي يتسم بالعدل والصواب، ويحكم بين الناس بصدق وعادلة، لا يشتري ولا يبيع، بل يعتمد على الحق والصواب في جميع الأمور، وهو من أهم صفات المؤمنين، والله سبحانه وتعالى يقول في القرآن الكريم: (وَمَن يُضِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن وَلِيٍّ بَعدَهُ) [النساء: 18]. والمقصود هنا هو أن الناقد هو الذي يُقيده الله على طاعة الله سبحانه وتعالى، ولا يترك له سوى الطاعة والقبول، فلا يُسمح له بالخروج عن حدود الله، ولا يُترك له سوى الطاعة والقبول، وبهذا يتم تحقيق العدل والصواب في العالم

in_urdu.name: ناقد
in_urdu.meaning: الجسماني یا عقلیہ طور پر انصاف یا صواب کا مُدقق، جس میں عادل و موازنہ ہو
in_urdu.long_meaning: ناقد، ایک اسامی جو اکثر اسے دوسروں میں انصاف کرنے والا یا عقلیہ طور پر انصاف کرنے والا کہا جاتا ہے۔ اس سے مراد وہ شخص جو اپنے اعمال اور کردار میں عادل ہو۔ اس کی علامت کا مطلب ہے کہ وہ کسی بھی صورت حال میں عادل و موازنہ ہے۔ اور یہی اس کے لیے ایک بہترین نام ہے۔

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Naqid' in the Islamic finance industry refers to an auditor or accountant who ensures the compliance of financial transactions with Sharia principles. In the modern context, Naqids play a crucial role in the Islamic finance industry, especially in platforms such as Mudarabah model, Sukuk bond, and Roskam Analytics. The Mudarabah model requires a Naqid to oversee the financial activities and investments of the Mudarib (entrepreneur) to ensure that they adhere to Sharia principles. In the case of Sukuk bonds, a Naqid is essential to certify the issuance and transaction of these bonds, which are backed by tangible assets and comply with Islamic law. Roskam Analytics, a leading provider of Sharia compliance services, employs a team of Naqids to assess and certify the Sharia compliance of various financial instruments, including Sukuk bonds, which are then listed on major stock exchanges. The increasing trend towards digitization in the financial sector is also impacting the role of Naqids. With the rise of fintech and digital transformation, many Islamic finance institutions are adopting digital platforms to streamline their operations and enhance their services. In this context, Naqids are increasingly required to have a strong understanding of digital technologies and their application in the Islamic finance industry. Overall, the role of Naqids in the Islamic finance industry is evolving, and they are becoming essential players in ensuring the compliance of financial transactions with Sharia principles in the digital age.
